docs.title: Caching Guide
docs.text: polars-baseball includes a file cache to avoid redundant network requests during large data queries.

docs.title: Caching Strategy
docs.text:
• Default status: Importing the package performs no cache I/O. The default file cache is initialized on the first cached request.
  • Storage location: File cache data is stored in the directory you configure. By default, it adheres to the XDG Base Directory specification: ~/.cache/polars_baseball (or $XDG_CACHE_HOME/polars_baseball) on Linux/macOS and %LOCALAPPDATA%/polars_baseball on Windows.
  • Storage format: Cached tables are written as Parquet for fast I/O and columnar compression.

docs.title: Programmatic Configuration
docs.text:
For explicit lifecycle control, create a file-backed BaseballClient:

from pathlib import Path
from polars_baseball import BaseballClient

client = BaseballClient.with_file_cache(Path("./my_project_cache"))

For package-level defaults, configure the POLARS_BASEBALL_CACHE_DIR environment variable before running your application:

export POLARS_BASEBALL_CACHE_DIR="./my_project_cache"

Use NullCacheAdapter for production services that need all caching controlled by the application. Use FileCacheAdapter when you want to inject a file cache directly:

from pathlib import Path
from polars_baseball import BaseballClient
from polars_baseball._cache import FileCacheAdapter, NullCacheAdapter
from polars_baseball._client import HttpClient

no_cache_client = BaseballClient(http=HttpClient(timeout=5.0, max_retries=0), cache=NullCacheAdapter())
file_cache_client = BaseballClient(cache=FileCacheAdapter(Path("./my_project_cache")))

Retries and BRef rate limiting are opt-in:

from polars_baseball import BaseballClient
from polars_baseball._client import HttpClient

client = BaseballClient(
    http=HttpClient(timeout=10.0, max_retries=2, bref_requests_per_minute=10),
)

Use context managers or explicit close() when a long-running script needs to manage HTTP clients cleanly:

import asyncio
from polars_baseball import BaseballClient

async def main() -> None:
    async with BaseballClient() as client:
        df = await client.mlb.schedule(2024)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Lifecycle & Concurrency in Web Services
docs.text:
For web services, always initialize and inject a custom BaseballClient tied to your application's lifecycle:

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import FastAPI
from polars_baseball import BaseballClient

# tied to lifespan
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.pb_client = BaseballClient.with_file_cache(Path("./service-cache"))
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        await app.state.pb_client.close()

POLARS_BASEBALL_CACHE_DIR configures the default cache directory for file-backed operations. Call BaseballClient.with_file_cache() to enable file caching explicitly.

docs.title: Cache Behavior
docs.text:
• Parameter-level matching: The cache key is based on the function, exact arguments, and cache schema version. Identical calls reuse cached results.
  • No subset matching: A cached query for statcast("2026-06-01", "2026-06-10") is not reused for statcast("2026-06-05", "2026-06-06").
  • Compiled datasets: Lahman and Chadwick Register tables are cached as per-table Parquet files under compiled-datasets/.
  • Compiled dataset CDN: Set POLARS_BASEBALL_DATASETS_URL to a hosted compiled dataset root. The client then downloads dataset/table.parquet files instead of compiling from upstream ZIP archives.

Internal gateway cache keys use generate_cache_key:

from polars_baseball._cache import generate_cache_key


def standings_cache_key(**kw: object) -> str:
    season = kw.get("season")
    return generate_cache_key("standings", {"season": season})

docs.text: [!NOTE] All public exceptions inherit from PolarsBaseballError. Inspecting exception types allows application logic to distinguish between invalid caller parameters and upstream service issues.

docs.title: Error Handling & Production Resilience
docs.text: This guide describes the exception hierarchy in polars_baseball, common error modes, and recommended patterns for handling errors in production services and data pipelines.

docs.title: Exception Hierarchy
docs.text:
All custom exceptions raised by polars_baseball are exported directly from polars_baseball (and defined in polars_baseball.exceptions) following a structured classification where 4xx client faults and 5xx server faults are strictly disjoint:

PolarsBaseballError (Base)
├── ClientError (4xx equivalent)
│   ├── InvalidParameterError
│   └── PolarsBaseballHttpClientError (HTTP 4xx; also PolarsBaseballHttpError)
├── ServerError (5xx equivalent)
│   ├── PolarsBaseballHttpServerError (HTTP 5xx; also PolarsBaseballHttpError)
│   ├── PolarsBaseballTransportError
│   ├── UpstreamParseError
│   │   ├── UpstreamStructureChangedError
│   │   └── UpstreamDataCorruptedError
│   ├── UpstreamUnavailableError
│   ├── InvalidSchemaError
│   └── CacheClearError
└── PolarsBaseballHttpError (HTTP base with .status_code and .retry_after)

docs.title: Exception Reference
docs.text: Exception Class Parent Trigger Scenario PolarsBaseballError Exception Base class for all package errors. ClientError PolarsBaseballError Caller error (invalid arguments or request payload). InvalidParameterError ClientError, ValueError Parameter validation failure (e.g. invalid date format or out-of-range season). PolarsBaseballHttpError PolarsBaseballError Base class for HTTP status errors (exposes .status_code and .retry_after). PolarsBaseballHttpClientError ClientError, PolarsBaseballHttpError HTTP 4xx client fault (e.g. status 403, 404). PolarsBaseballHttpServerError ServerError, PolarsBaseballHttpError HTTP 5xx upstream server fault (e.g. status 500, 502, 503). ServerError PolarsBaseballError Upstream network, HTTP 5xx, or parser failure. PolarsBaseballTransportError ServerError Network connection failure, timeout, or DNS resolution failure. UpstreamParseError ServerError, RuntimeError Failed to parse upstream response body (HTML/JSON). UpstreamStructureChangedError UpstreamParseError Upstream web layout or JSON payload schema changed. UpstreamDataCorruptedError UpstreamParseError Downloaded data payload is malformed or incomplete. UpstreamUnavailableError ServerError Upstream service returned an empty response or maintenance notice. InvalidSchemaError ServerError Polars schema validation mismatch. CacheClearError ServerError File cache deletion or write error.

docs.title: Basic Error Handling Pattern
docs.text:
Use standard Python try...except blocks to handle caller errors vs. transient upstream network issues separately:

import asyncio
from polars_baseball import BaseballClient
from polars_baseball.exceptions import (
    ClientError,
    PolarsBaseballHttpError,
    PolarsBaseballTransportError,
    ServerError,
)

async def fetch_data() -> None:
    client = BaseballClient()
    try:
        df = await client.savant.statcast(start_date="2026-06-01", end_date="2026-06-02")
        print(f"Retrieved {df.height} rows.")
    except ClientError as err:
        print(f"Invalid caller request: {err}")
    except PolarsBaseballHttpError as err:
        print(f"HTTP Error {err.status_code}: {err}")
    except PolarsBaseballTransportError as err:
        print(f"Network connectivity error: {err}")
    except ServerError as err:
        print(f"Upstream server error: {err}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(fetch_data())

docs.title: Production Retry Strategy
docs.text:
When running automated pipelines or web endpoints, transient upstream errors (such as HTTP 502/503 or network timeouts) should be retried with exponential backoff.

[!TIP] Do not retry ClientError or InvalidParameterError as caller errors will fail consistently without parameter changes.

import asyncio
import logging
from typing import TypeVar, Callable, Awaitable
import polars_baseball as pb
from polars_baseball.exceptions import ClientError, ServerError

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

T = TypeVar("T")

async def retry_async(
    func: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]],
    max_retries: int = 3,
    initial_delay: float = 1.0,
    backoff_factor: float = 2.0,
) -> T:
    delay = initial_delay
    for attempt in range(1, max_retries + 1):
        try:
            return await func()
        except ClientError:
            raise  # Do not retry invalid input errors
        except ServerError as err:
            if attempt == max_retries:
                logger.error("Final retry failed for upstream query.", exc_info=True)
                raise
            logger.warning(
                "Attempt %d/%d failed with error (%s). Retrying in %.1fs...",
                attempt, max_retries, err, delay
            )
            await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            delay *= backoff_factor
    raise RuntimeError("Unreachable")

async def main() -> None:
    async with pb.BaseballClient() as client:
        df = await retry_async(
            lambda: client.savant.statcast(start_date="2026-06-01", end_date="2026-06-01")
        )
        print("Success, rows:", df.height)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Managing Session Resources in Web Applications
docs.text:
In long-running web services (e.g. FastAPI, Starlette), wrap calls with BaseballClient to share connection pools, manage timeouts, and cleanly handle resource cleanup on shutdown.

from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
import polars_baseball as pb
from polars_baseball.exceptions import ClientError, ServerError

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    async with pb.BaseballClient() as client:
        app.state.pb_client = client
        yield

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

@app.get("/api/schedule")
async def get_schedule(date: str):
    client: pb.BaseballClient = app.state.pb_client
    try:
        df = await client.mlb.schedule(date=date)
        return {"count": df.height, "data": df.to_dicts()}
    except ClientError as err:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(err))
    except ServerError as err:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail=f"Upstream provider failure: {err}")

class BRefClient:
    """Namespaced Baseball Reference client."""

    def __init__(self, client: BaseballClient) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._gateway = BRefGateway(client)

    async def _bwar_generic(
        self,
        stat_type: Literal["bat", "pitch"],
        required_cols: list[str],
        col_types: dict[str, pl.DataType | type[pl.DataType]],
        all_columns: bool = False,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        return await self._gateway.get_bwar(stat_type, required_cols, col_types, all_columns=all_columns)

    async def bwar_bat(self, all_columns: bool = False) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Fetch batting WAR from Baseball Reference."""
        return await self._bwar_generic("bat", BWAR_BAT_REQUIRED, BWAR_BAT_TYPES, all_columns=all_columns)

    async def bwar_pitch(self, all_columns: bool = False) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Fetch pitching WAR from Baseball Reference."""
        return await self._bwar_generic("pitch", BWAR_PITCH_REQUIRED, BWAR_PITCH_TYPES, all_columns=all_columns)

    async def game_logs(
        self,
        player_id: str,
        year: int,
        log_type: Literal["batting", "pitching"] = "batting",
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Fetch Baseball Reference single-season game logs for a player."""
        if not player_id:
            raise InvalidParameterError("player_id must not be empty.")
        if log_type not in ("batting", "pitching"):
            raise InvalidParameterError("log_type must be either 'batting' or 'pitching'.")
        return await self._gateway.get_game_logs(player_id, year, log_type)

    async def splits(
        self,
        player_id: str,
        year: int | None = None,
        pitching: bool = False,
    ) -> list[pl.DataFrame]:
        """Fetch Baseball Reference platoon/situational splits for a player."""
        if not player_id:
            raise InvalidParameterError("player_id must not be empty.")
        df_main, player_info, df_level = await self._gateway.get_splits(player_id, year, pitching)
        df_info = pl.DataFrame(
            {
                "Position": [player_info.get("Position", "")],
                "Bats": [player_info.get("Bats", "")],
                "Throws": [player_info.get("Throws", "")],
            }
        )
        return [df_main, df_info, df_level]

    async def _execute_fg_query(
        self,
        start_season: int,
        *,
        end_season: int | None = None,
        stats_category: str | FangraphsStatsCategory = FangraphsStatsCategory.BATTING,
        league: str | FangraphsLeague = FangraphsLeague.ALL,
        month: str | FangraphsMonth = FangraphsMonth.ALL,
        position: str | FangraphsPositions = FangraphsPositions.ALL,
        stat_columns: str | list[str] | list[FangraphsStatColumn] = "ALL",
        qual: int | None = None,
        split_seasons: bool = True,
        ind: int = 1,
        on_active_roster: bool = False,
        minimum_age: int = 0,
        maximum_age: int = 100,
        team: str = "",

        players: str = "",
        max_results: int = FG_MAX_RESULTS,
        is_team_data: bool = False,
        force_update: bool = False,
        cache_max_age: timedelta | None = None,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        resolved_end_season = start_season if end_season is None else end_season

        resolved_league = _resolve_league(league)
        resolved_month = _resolve_month(month)
        resolved_position = _resolve_position(position)
        resolved_columns = stat_list_from_str(resolved_category, stat_columns)

        _validate_enum_field(resolved_category, FangraphsStatsCategory, "stats_category")
        _validate_enum_field(resolved_league, FangraphsLeague, "league")
        _validate_enum_field(resolved_month, FangraphsMonth, "month")
        _validate_enum_field(resolved_position, FangraphsPositions, "position")
        _validate_list_of_enum(resolved_columns, FangraphsStatsBase, "stat_columns")

        coerced_filters = [FanGraphsFilter.coerce(f) for f in filters] if filters else []

        options = _build_fg_url_options(
            start_season=start_season,
            end_season=resolved_end_season,
            category=resolved_category,
            league=resolved_league,
            month=resolved_month,
            position=resolved_position,
            stat_columns=resolved_columns,
            qual=qual,
            split_seasons=split_seasons,
            ind=ind,
            on_active_roster=on_active_roster,
            minimum_age=minimum_age,
            maximum_age=maximum_age,
            team=team,
            filters=coerced_filters,
            players=players,
            max_results=max_results,
            is_team_data=is_team_data,
        )

        effective_max_age = _resolve_fg_cache_max_age(resolved_end_season, cache_max_age)
        df = await self._gateway.get_leaderboard(
            FG_LEADERS_URL,
            options,
            max_age=effective_max_age,
            force_update=force_update,
        )
        return _apply_filters(df, coerced_filters)

class LookupClient:
    """Namespaced Player and Team lookup client."""

    def __init__(self, client: BaseballClient) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._gateway = CompiledDatasetGateway(client)
        self._service = PlayerLookupService(lambda _ctx: self.get_lookup_table(save=True))

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """Reset cached player lookup table in memory."""
        self._service.reset()

    async def chadwick_register(self, save: bool = True) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Fetch the raw Chadwick Baseball Register dataset."""
        logger.info("Gathering player lookup table from Chadwick register gateway.")
        raw = await self._gateway.read_table(_chadwick_people_table(), use_cache=save)
        return _normalize_chadwick_register(raw)

    async def get_lookup_table(self, save: bool = True) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Fetch the Chadwick register with lowercased name_last and name_first columns."""
        table = await self.chadwick_register(save=save)
        if table.is_empty():
            return table
        return table.with_columns(
            pl.col("name_last").str.to_lowercase(),
            pl.col("name_first").str.to_lowercase(),
        )

    async def playerid_lookup(
        self,
        last: str,
        first: str | None = None,
        ignore_accents: bool = False,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Lookup a player by last (and optionally first) name."""
        df = await self._service.search(last, first, ignore_accents, client=self._client)
        if df.is_empty():
            warnings.warn(
                "No player found for the given name. Check the spelling or use "
                "client.lookup.player_name_suggestions(last, first) for fuzzy matches.",
                UserWarning,
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        return df

    async def player_name_suggestions(
        self,
        last: str,
        first: str | None = None,
        ignore_accents: bool = False,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Return fuzzy player name suggestions without treating them as exact lookup results."""
        return await self._service.suggest(last, first, ignore_accents, client=self._client)

    async def player_search_list(
        self,
        player_list: list[tuple[str, str]],
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Batch lookup for multiple player name pairs."""
        return await self._service.search_list(player_list, client=self._client)

    async def playerid_reverse_lookup(
        self,
        player_ids: list[PlayerId],
        key_type: KeyType = KeyType.MLBAM,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Reverse lookup players by their IDs in a given key system."""
        return await self._service.reverse_lookup(player_ids, key_type, client=self._client)

    def team_ids(self, season: int | None = None, league: str = "ALL") -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Fetch team identifiers from bundled FanGraphs team data."""
        return _read_team_ids(season=season, league=league)

class RetrosheetClient:
    """Namespaced Retrosheet client."""

    def __init__(self, client: BaseballClient) -> None:
        self._client = client
        self._gateway = RetrosheetGateway(client)

    async def events(
        self,
        season: int,
        game_type: str = "regular",
        force_update: bool = False,
        *,
        concurrency_limit: int = 5,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:
        """Fetch Retrosheet event files for a given season."""
        if game_type not in _RETROSHEET_GAME_TYPE_EXTENSIONS:
            raise InvalidParameterError(
                f"Illegal type argument {game_type}, the valid types are: 'regular', 'post', and 'asg'."
            )

        async def _fetch_events() -> pl.DataFrame:
            files = await self._gateway.get_season_contents(season)
            file_extensions = _RETROSHEET_GAME_TYPE_EXTENSIONS[game_type]

            season_events = [t for t in files if t.endswith(file_extensions)]
            if not season_events:
                raise ServerError(f"Event files not available for {season}")

            async def _fetch_event(filename: str) -> dict[str, object]:
                raw = await self._gateway.get_event_file(season, filename)
                return event_content_row(season, game_type, filename, raw)

            tasks = [lambda f=f: _fetch_event(f) for f in season_events]
            results = await bounded_gather(tasks, concurrency_limit=concurrency_limit)
            rows = [row for row in results if row is not None]
            return events_frame(rows)

        key = generate_cache_key("retrosheet/events", {"season": season, "game_type": game_type})
        return await self._client.cache.get_or_fetch(key, _fetch_events, force_update=force_update)

    async def rosters(
        self,

        force_update: bool = False,
        *,
        concurrency_limit: int = 5,
    ) -> pl.DataFrame:

            files = await self._gateway.get_season_contents(season)

docs.title: Semantic Versioning Guarantees
docs.text:
polars-baseball adheres to Semantic Versioning 2.0.0.

Given a version number MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: - MAJOR version bumps indicate breaking changes to the stable SDK interface. - MINOR version bumps indicate backwards-compatible feature additions or deprecation announcements. - PATCH version bumps indicate backwards-compatible bug fixes and upstream parser adaptations.

docs.title: SDK Surface Stability
docs.text:
The following SDK components constitute the stable public interface:

  1. Client Lifecycle & Namespaces:
  2. BaseballClient instantiation, configuration parameters (http, cache, cache_dir, github_token), and context manager lifecycle (__aenter__, __aexit__, close(), aclose()).
  3. Provider namespace accessors: client.savant, client.mlb, client.fangraphs, client.bref, client.retrosheet, client.lahman, and client.lookup.

docs.title: Upstream Data Drift Policy
docs.text:
polars-baseball retrieves data from third-party and unofficial baseball data providers (MLB Stats API, Baseball Savant, FanGraphs, Baseball Reference, and Retrosheet). Upstream providers occasionally modify unannounced response formats or deprecate metrics without notice.

To balance SDK reliability with real-world sports data dynamics:

docs.title: 1. Tier-1: Core Identity Columns (Guaranteed)
docs.text: Core entity identifiers, dates, and primary keys are guaranteed across minor releases: - Player identity keys: player_id, mlbam_id, key_mlbam, key_fangraphs, key_bbref. - Game identity keys: game_pk, game_date, season. - Base tabular structure: output always resolves to a valid tabular polars.DataFrame or empty DataFrame with typed schema.

docs.title: 2. Tier-2: Upstream Raw Metrics (Drift Tolerant)
docs.text: Advanced metrics, tracking attributes, and provider-specific calculation fields (e.g., newly added Statcast bat tracking metrics, modified Statcast column names such as spin_rate_deprecated, or FanGraphs custom leaderboard columns): - Upstream additions or removals of secondary metric columns do not constitute a breaking change for the library. - When an upstream provider alters, drops, or renames raw columns, polars-baseball adapts parser schemas and normalization pipelines in patch or minor releases. - Schema conflicts across heterogeneous date queries are automatically coalesced and normalized without data loss.

docs.title: Provider Service Levels & Best-Effort Scrapers
docs.text: polars-baseball categorizes data providers into two distinct operational tiers:

docs.title: Tier 1: Structured APIs & Compiled Archives (High Reliability)
docs.text:
• MLB Stats API (client.mlb.*), Baseball Savant (client.savant.*), Retrosheet (client.retrosheet.*), and Lahman (client.lahman.*).
  • These providers offer structured JSON, CSV, or archival data endpoints without active anti-bot gates. They are considered highly reliable for automated data pipelines.

docs.title: Tier 2: Unofficial Web Scrapers (Best-Effort & Anti-Bot Protected)
docs.text:
• FanGraphs (client.fangraphs.*) and Baseball Reference (client.bref.*).
  • These providers rely on HTML table parsing and undocumented internal query endpoints. Both sites employ Cloudflare Turnstile anti-bot protection and strict rate limiting.
  • Service Level Guarantee: Access to Tier 2 sources is provided strictly on a best-effort basis. Users must respect provider Terms of Service, configure conservative rate limits (bref_requests_per_minute), pass clearance tokens via extra_headers (CF_CLEARANCE, CF_COOKIE) when prompted, or rely on local parquet cache. Uninterrupted availability cannot be guaranteed if upstream anti-bot policies change.

docs.title: Deprecation Lifecycle
docs.text:
When a public API method or parameter is scheduled for deprecation:

  1. Announcement: The symbol raises a DeprecationWarning (stacklevel=2) explaining the replacement method and scheduled removal version.
  2. Horizon: Deprecated symbols will survive for at least one minor release before removal.
  3. Changelog: All deprecations and removals are documented under the Deprecated and Removed sections of CHANGELOG.md following the Keep a Changelog standard.

docs.title: Statcast & Savant
docs.text: [!NOTE] All public data-fetching APIs are asynchronous. Use await inside an async environment, or asyncio.run() in scripts.

docs.title: Baseball Savant / Statcast
docs.text:
Access Statcast pitch-level queries, leaderboards, park factors, gamefeeds, and local partitioned Parquet datasets via savant.SavantClient (client.savant).

[!TIP] Need a player's key_mlbam? Use await client.lookup.playerid_lookup("Judge", "Aaron").

docs.title: Local Partitioned Dataset (sync_statcast / scan_statcast)
docs.text:
sync_statcast scrapes full seasons into {cache_dir}/compiled-datasets/statcast/year={year}/statcast.parquet, and scan_statcast returns a pl.LazyFrame with predicate and projection pushdown.

[!NOTE] scan_statcast raises UpstreamUnavailableError when a requested season has no local partition and auto_download=False. Requires a file-backed cache directory (BaseballClient(cache_dir=Path) or default cache).

docs.title: Spray Angle Calculation
docs.text:
Calculate spray angles directly with Polars expressions or Python math:

from math import atan2, pi

hc_x, hc_y = 125.42, 198.27
spray_angle = atan2(hc_x - 125.42, 198.27 - hc_y) * 180 / pi

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
import asyncio
from polars_baseball import BaseballClient


async def main() -> None:
    async with BaseballClient() as client:
        pitches = await client.savant.statcast(start_date="2026-06-01", end_date="2026-06-01")
        expected = await client.savant.expected_stats(2026, player_type="batter", min_pa=100)
        print(pitches.head(2), expected.head(2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
